classification.difficultyReason: Apply axis reflections and an origin rotation to supplied graph landmarks, then explain which zero sets remain unchanged and recognise when the rotated graph coincides with the original. Earlier sketches scaffold these routine linked interpretations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The graph of an unknown function $y=f(x)$ has been drawn on the right.

spec.description: Unknown smooth curve reconstructed with its source landmarks, turning points, arrows and dashed guides. The interpolating path supplies no equation.
spec.mathematics: Zeroes 0 and 3; local maximum (1,2); point (2,1); local minimum (3,0).

children.label: i
children.prompt: Which reflection produces $y=f(-x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.worked: Map each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,y)$. The maximum becomes $(-1,2)$, $(2,1)$ becomes $(-2,1)$, and the zeroes become $x=-3,0$.

spec.description: Horizontal reflection of the unknown source curve.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Which reflection produces $y=-f(x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.worked: Map each point $(x,y)$ to $(x,-y)$. The maximum becomes a minimum at $(1,-2)$, $(2,1)$ becomes $(2,-1)$, and the zeroes remain $x=0,3$.

spec.description: Vertical reflection of the unknown source curve.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Compare the zeroes of $f(x)$, $f(-x)$ and $-f(x)$. Which pair have the same zeroes, and why?

answer.short: $f(x)$ and $-f(x)$ both have zeroes $x=0,3$. The zeroes of $f(-x)$ are $x=-3,0$. Reflection in the $x$-axis preserves zeroes.
answer.worked: A zero is a point with $y=0$. Reflection in the $x$-axis sends $(x,0)$ to $(x,0)$, so $f(x)$ and $-f(x)$ retain zeroes $0,3$. Reflection in the $y$-axis changes each zero $x$ to $-x$, giving $-3,0$ for $f(-x)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The graph of an unknown function $y=P(x)$ has been drawn on the right.

spec.description: Straight left branch joined at (0,1) to a smooth curved right branch; source guides and labels retained.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Which transformation produces $y=-P(x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.worked: Use $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$. The join becomes $(0,-1)$, the curved branch touches the axis at $(1,0)$ and passes through $(2,-1)$. Both zeroes, $-1$ and $1$, remain fixed.

spec.description: Reflected two-branch graph with unchanged zeroes.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Which transformation produces $y=-P(-x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.short: A $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin, equivalent to reflection in both axes.
answer.worked: Use $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$. The curved branch is now on the left through $(-2,-1)$ and $(-1,0)$, joining the straight right branch at $(0,-1)$. The straight branch crosses at $(1,0)$.

spec.description: Source graph rotated through 180 degrees about the origin.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: In this case, $P(x)$ and $-P(-x)$ both have the same zeroes. Why might that be?

answer.short: The zeroes $-1$ and $1$ are symmetric about the origin, so a $180^\circ$ rotation interchanges them.
answer.worked: The rotation sends $(-1,0)$ to $(1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ to $(-1,0)$. Therefore the set of zeroes remains $\{-1,1\}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The graph of an unknown function $y=A(x)$ has been drawn on the right.

spec.description: Origin-symmetric S-shaped unknown curve with its asymptotes and coordinate guides. The interpolating path supplies no equation.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Which transformation produces $y=A(-x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.worked: Use $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$. The reflected graph decreases through $(-1,1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,-1)$, with horizontal asymptotes $y=2$ and $y=-2$.

spec.description: Decreasing S-shaped reflected curve with both asymptotes and coordinate guides.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Which transformation produces $y=-A(-x)$? Draw the graph of this function.

answer.short: A $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin, equivalent to reflection in both axes.
answer.worked: Use $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$. The points $(-1,-1)$ and $(1,1)$ interchange, and the origin remains fixed. The horizontal asymptotes interchange. The resulting graph coincides with $y=A(x)$.

spec.description: Rotated graph coinciding with the original S-shaped graph.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Explain why the zeroes of all three functions are the same in this instance.

answer.short: The sole zero is $x=0$, which is fixed by these reflections and rotations.
answer.worked: The original graph crosses the axes only at $(0,0)$. Reflection in the $y$-axis and rotation about the origin both fix this point, so each graph has the sole zero $x=0$.

children.label: iv
children.prompt: What do you notice about the graphs of $y=A(x)$ and $y=-A(-x)$?

answer.worked: The graph has rotational symmetry of $180^\circ$ about the origin, so $-A(-x)=A(x)$.
